title: Showmob artifact status board: draft, in PR, published
summary: Where every artifact stands in the pipeline, and what moves it to the next column.

blocks.title: The pipeline, three columns
blocks.body: Every Showmob artifact lives in exactly one state: draft (still being worked), preview (in or past a PR, visible by direct link only), or published (listed, live, meant for anyone). The board below is the operating picture, with example counts from a working day.

blocks.heading: Status board (example snapshot)
rows: Local work, Studio experiments, half-finished pages
An agent or author saves it as preview and opens a PR
Grading-night batches awaiting merge, pages under review
CI goes green and the PR merges - it is then live but unlisted
The guide, the courses, the plan series
Rarely leaves; archived only when superseded
blocks.caption: Preview pages render at their direct URL but never appear on Home. Unlisted is not private - anyone with the link sees them.

blocks.heading: How to read the board at a glance
blocks.body: The number that matters is the middle column. Drafts are cheap and published pages are done; the PR column is where work waits. A board with twelve items in PR for more than a day means review is the bottleneck, not writing. A board with nothing in draft means nobody is starting anything. Healthy flow shows motion, not any particular count.

items.label: Sweep the PR column
items.detail: Anything green merges; anything red gets fixed or closed. Nothing rots open.

items.label: Check preview pages are not linked publicly
items.detail: Preview is for review and grading. If a preview link lands somewhere public, that is a publishing decision made by accident.

items.label: Promote deliberately
items.detail: Preview to published is a human call, per artifact, after it has been read like a reader.

blocks.title: Why 'in PR' is its own column
blocks.body: Merging is not the moment an artifact gets real - the PR is. It is the first time the page renders on the real site for anyone with the link, the first time CI validates it, the first time it can be graded. Treating the PR column as first-class keeps the pipeline honest about where work actually sits.
